title: Find Duplicate Customer Emails
description:
Find email addresses that belong to **more than one customer** (duplicates). Return the email and how many times it appears.

**Table: customers**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| id | INT |
| name | VARCHAR |
| email | VARCHAR |
| city | VARCHAR |
| country | VARCHAR |

Output columns: `email`, `count`. Order by `count` descending, then `email`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INT, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, country VARCHAR); INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Alice','alice@example.com','New York','USA'),(2,'Bob','bob@example.com','London','UK'),(3,'Carol','alice@example.com','Chicago','USA'),(4,'Dan','dan@example.com','Mumbai','India'),(5,'Eve','bob@example.com','Paris','France'),(6,'Fay','bob@example.com','Berlin','Germany');
solution_sql: SELECT email, COUNT(*) AS count FROM customers GROUP BY email HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY count DESC, email

test_cases.description: bob@example.com appears 3 times; alice@example.com appears 2 times

hints: GROUP BY email, then HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 filters to only duplicated emails.
This is the standard duplicate detection pattern.
explanation: `GROUP BY email` collapses all rows with the same email. `HAVING COUNT(*) > 1` keeps only those with 2+ rows. bob@example.com (count 3) and alice@example.com (count 2) are duplicates.
